identityReview: Mohammed VI, king of Morocco and son of Hassan II, born Rabat August 21, 1963. Distinguish him from grandfather Mohammed V and other similarly named monarchs. Accession July 23, 1999 differs from first throne speech/annual celebration July 30. Official biographies agree on 1993 Nice law doctorate; 1988 qualification wording differs, so no additional doctorate asserted. George Washington University 2000 degree is honorary. Current king, not prime minister; government changed to El Mansouri in 2026 while royal office continued.
lifeStatusEvidence: Completed October 14, 2026 official audience, October 16 new-minister swearing-in independently reported by Le Monde, and November 4 Royal Office/MAP report of king-chairing Rabat working session. These establish recent reported personal activity rather than future diary entries. Photo/video pixels not inspected.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read relevant French and English official biography sections; official constitutional articles and referendum chronology; Brookings analysis and HRW historical reporting; World Bank background/methodology excerpts; AU communiqué; railway participant inauguration report; recent official appointment/audience/working-session statements and Le Monde substantive event report. Portrait metadata and original Flickr licence link read, no portrait pixels.
corrections: Read relevant French official biography paragraphs: Rabat August 21, 1963; 1985 licence in law; 1988 Brussels traineeship with Jacques Delors; October 29, 1993 Nice–Sophia Antipolis law doctorate on EEC–Maghreb cooperation. French July 1988 wording is diplôme des études supérieures du doctorat en droit public, not independently verified completion of an additional doctorate. July 23, 1999 accession follows Hassan II death; July 30 first Throne Day address is a distinct event.

Read English official biography and degree/award entries. It calls the July 1988 qualification a doctorate, unlike the more specific French wording; do not count a second doctorate. Both agree on 1985 law degree and 1993 Nice doctorate. English entry explicitly records George Washington University honorary doctorate June 22, 2000. Official institutional wording is attributed biographical evidence, not independent authentication of original diplomas or birth documents. Decorative praise is not reproduced.

Read relevant official 2011 Constitution sections: articles 41 and 42 separate religious and head-of-state functions; article 47 appointment from the party leading House of Representatives elections; article 48 council presidency; article 53 armed-forces supreme command. Royal decree dated July 29, 2011 differs from July 1 referendum and July 30 official-gazette issue. No assertion the constitution removed substantive royal authority or made king and head of government identical.

Read official constitutional referendum chronology explicitly listing July 1, 2011. It supports referendum date; promulgation comes from the official text, and political context from Brookings. Do not treat listing of a referendum as an independent audit of turnout, result percentages or electoral fairness.

Read substantive sections of Brookings 2020 analysis on reforms, family law, political authority, rural–urban differences and repression. Family-law change in 2004 and 2011 reform context are historical; analytic judgments are attributed, not presented as unanimous findings or fresh 2026 measurements. No causal claim that the king alone built every project, no current poverty/unemployment statistics and no forecast treated as an accomplished event.

Read Human Rights Watch World Report 2026 country chapter explicitly labelled Events of 2025: criticism of repression of protesters/critics and family-code inequalities and exceptions. Attribute rights assessments to HRW; publication year does not turn described 2025 events into 2026 events. Discussion of subsequent family-code proposals is historical as of the report; no claim to have audited current November 2026 enactment status, all court files or each allegation.

Read relevant background/methodology paragraphs of World Bank-hosted INDH impact study: royal announcement May 18, 2005, main programme launch September 2005, phases and targeted services. Evaluation uses 2008/2011/2013 surveys with design restrictions. Canonical text only adopts launch and programme scope; no nationwide poverty-elimination claim, causal effect estimate or proof every beneficiary target was met.

Read AU January 31, 2017 closing communiqué documenting Morocco admission/readmission at the 28th summit and actual address by Mohammed VI. Use month precision for the membership milestone rather than equating communiqué date and decision date. Morocco joining the AU/restoring participation in the pan-African institutional framework does not establish a final Western Sahara settlement. Do not infer later incumbencies of AU officials from this historical release.

Read SYSTRA November 15, 2018 inauguration report: king and Emmanuel Macron aboard Al Boraq, new Tangier–Kenitra high-speed infrastructure and services continuing via Rabat to Casablanca. Distinguish new high-speed section from whole service route. Contractor is a project participant; its commercial praise, passenger forecasts and claimed budget performance are not independent audited outcomes. No specific route-length figure adopted where other reports differ.

Read official September 29, 2026 completed audience and appointment statement: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, coordinator of PAM collective leadership, appointed head of government and tasked with forming it under article 47. Do not equate designation with already completed cabinet, parliamentary confidence or replacement of the monarch. Generic party-leader description avoids falsely asserting sole presidency of collective leadership.

Read October 14, 2026 official completed audience at Rabat Royal Palace, with head of government tasked with formation reporting progress. This is an actual event, not a planned audience or evidence the cabinet had already been sworn in that day. Wishes for successful government action are not achieved policy outcomes.

Read Le Monde October 17, 2026 headline, substantive lead and body rendered by search tool despite subscriber/gift UI: 32 ministers sworn before the king on Friday October 16. Canonical text uses the occurrence/date only, without minister-by-minister claims, a claim of equal representation or completed confidence vote. The article describes handover/next parliamentary steps separately; no schedule is converted into a completed event.

Read Royal Office/MAP November 4, 2026 statement identifying actual king-chaired working session at Rabat Royal Palace and participants including El Mansouri. Western Sahara sovereignty, autonomy, ceasefire and mission assessments are positions of a party to the dispute. Canonical text uses meeting and attributed policy position, not the statement as proof of final internationally settled sovereignty or a fully independently audited UN mission-closure chronology.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial/translation review, not certified human or native-language review. No original birth certificate or degree authentication, exhaustive legal/history audit, latest family-code legislative docket, project-finance/outcome audit, independent investigation of each rights allegation or portrait pixels. HRW report covers 2025; Brookings analysis dates from 2020. Royal Western Sahara positions remain attributed, not accepted as final international adjudication. Parliamentary confidence and future arrangements not inferred solely from cabinet appointment.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against Chinese and English: 1963 Rabat birth, 1985 law degree, 1988 training/qualification ambiguity, 1993 academic doctorate versus 2000 honorary degree; July 23 accession versus July 30 throne commemoration; separate monarch/head-of-government offices; 2004 family-code reform versus later proposals; May 18, 2005 INDH announcement versus implementation/outcomes; July 1, 2011 referendum versus July 29 promulgation and retained royal powers; January 2017 AU admission without implying territorial settlement; November 15, 2018 Tangier–Kenitra high-speed section versus extended service; September 29, October 14/16 and November 4, 2026 completed events; attributed Western Sahara positions and HRW 2026 report describing 2025.
